questions.q: Which zone typically hosts public-facing servers while protecting the internal network?
questions.explain: The DMZ is the buffer zone where public services are exposed without directly exposing the internal zone.

questions.q: A control must observe traffic without ever blocking it. Which placement should be chosen?
questions.explain: A detective IDS receives a copy of traffic via SPAN/tap: it is out-of-path and cannot block.

questions.q: Which signals does a Zero Trust architecture verify before granting access? (Select all that apply)
options: Device membership in the asset inventory
questions.explain: Zero Trust verifies the user, device health, inventory status, and application control — not just network location.

questions.q: Which failure mode prioritizes service availability?
questions.explain: In fail-open mode, traffic passes if the control fails: availability takes priority, at the risk of bypass.

questions.q: Match each mechanism to its role.

pairs.right: Single entry point for out-of-band administration
Cloud security services close to the user

questions.explain: SSE and gMSA are exam-objective concepts absent from the provided textbooks.

questions.q: A user changes roles and retains their old administrative rights. What is this situation called?
questions.explain: Privilege creep is the accumulation of unrevoked rights; the countermeasure is periodic access reviews.
